To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
• Accuracy is a metric that is widely used and easy to understand.
the most useful metrics are: accuracy, precision, recall, f1-score, confusion matrix, AUC, ROC curve and lift chart.
• the best metrics to compare two models are accuracy, F1 score, AUC and Cohen’s Kappa • the best metrics for analysing the behaviour and tuning of a single model are accuracy, precision and recall
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: Which metrics are most useful in multi-class classification? How do they differ? How to choose the most suitable one? How to use them in practice?
the following questions: Which multi-class metrics exist? How do they work? What is their usage? Which metric is the most appropriate in a certain context?

the following questions: Which metrics are most appropriate to evaluate the performance of a multi-class classification model? How can they be applied to compare different models or to analyse the behaviour of the model?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best metric for a multi-class problem is not one metric, but a combination of different metrics.
the best metric to be used in a multi-class classification task depends on the problem at hand.

no single metric can provide all the information needed to evaluate a multi-class classifier, but the combination of multiple metrics can provide a more accurate picture of the performance of the classifier.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is not a single metric which fits all needs.
, for the multi-class case, metrics can be grouped in three categories: metrics based on the confusion matrix, metrics based on the ROC curve and metrics based on the cost matrix.
the best metric for the evaluation of a multi-class classification task is the one that is the most suitable for the particular task.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of the metric to use should depend on the specific task and on the type of data at hand, as well as on the specific stage in the machine learning process.
the choice of a metric is a critical step of the machine learning process.
the choice of the performance metric should be driven by the specific task and by the nature of the data.
